Here’s a significantly more advanced Keras project designed for a seasoned engineer like you: it implements a Graph Neural Network (GNN) using Graph Attention Networks (GAT) in Keras, trained on a citation dataset for node classification. It’s markedly different, tackling graphs, attention, and deep embedding—far beyond typical CNN or VAE workflows.

Project Title

ai-ml-ds-VaZnkfTgQwL – Graph Attention Network for Citation Node Classification
File: graph_attention_citation_classification.py

import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras import Model, optimizers, losses, metrics
from tensorflow.keras.layers import Layer, Dropout, Dense, Input
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
import networkx as nx

# Hyperparameters
n_heads: int = 8
hidden_units: int = 8
dropout_rate: float = 0.6
learning_rate: float = 0.005
epochs: int = 200
patience: int = 20

# Load Cora dataset via tf.keras utility
import tensorflow_datasets as tfds
dataset = tfds.load("cora", as_supervised=False)
data = tfds.as_numpy(dataset["train"])

# Parse graph
Gnx = nx.DiGraph()
features: np.ndarray = data["node_features"]
labels_str = data["node_label"]
labels_enc = LabelEncoder().fit(labels_str)
labels: np.ndarray = labels_enc.transform(labels_str)
edges_src = data["edge_source"]
edges_dst = data["edge_target"]
for u, v in zip(edges_src, edges_dst):
    Gnx.add_edge(int(u), int(v))
n_nodes: int = features.shape[0]
n_feats: int = features.shape[1]
n_classes: int = len(labels_enc.classes_)

# Adjacency normalization
A = nx.adjacency_matrix(Gnx).astype(np.float32)
A = A + np.eye(n_nodes)
deg = np.array(A.sum(1)).flatten()
D_12 = np.power(deg, -0.5)
D_12 = np.diag(D_12)
A_norm: np.ndarray = D_12 @ A.toarray() @ D_12

# Train/test split
idx = np.arange(n_nodes)
idx_train, idx_test = train_test_split(idx, stratify=labels, train_size=0.6, random_state=42)
y_train = tf.one_hot(labels[idx_train], depth=n_classes)
y_test = tf.one_hot(labels[idx_test], depth=n_classes)

# Graph Attention layer
class GraphAttention(Layer):
    def __init__(self, F_out, n_heads=1, dropout=0.6, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.F_out = F_out
        self.n_heads = n_heads
        self.dropout = dropout

    def build(self, input_shape):
        self.W = self.add_weight(shape=(input_shape[-1], self.F_out * self.n_heads),
                                  initializer="glorot_uniform", name="W")
        self.a_src = self.add_weight(shape=(self.n_heads, self.F_out), initializer="glorot_uniform", name="a_src")
        self.a_dst = self.add_weight(shape=(self.n_heads, self.F_out), initializer="glorot_uniform", name="a_dst")
        super().build(input_shape)

    def call(self, X, A):
        h = tf.matmul(X, self.W)  # (N, F_out*heads)
        h = tf.reshape(h, (-1, self.n_heads, self.F_out))  # (N, heads, F_out)
        attn_src = tf.tensordot(h, self.a_src, axes=[[2],[1]])  # (N, heads)
        attn_dst = tf.tensordot(h, self.a_dst, axes=[[2],[1]])  # (N, heads)
        attn = attn_src[:,None,:,:] + attn_dst[None,:,:,:]
        attn = tf.nn.leaky_relu(attn)
        attn = tf.where(A[:,:,None]>0, attn, -9e15*tf.ones_like(attn))
        alpha = tf.nn.softmax(attn, axis=1)
        outputs = tf.reduce_mean(alpha * h[None,:,:,:], axis=1)
        return outputs

# Build model
X_in = Input(shape=(n_feats,), name="X_in")
A_in = Input((n_nodes,), sparse=False, name="A_in")
x = Dropout(dropout_rate)(X_in)
x = GraphAttention(hidden_units, n_heads, dropout_rate)(x, A_in)
x = Dropout(dropout_rate)(x)
x = GraphAttention(n_classes, 1, dropout_rate)(x, A_in)
output = tf.nn.log_softmax(x, axis=-1)
model = Model(inputs=[X_in, A_in], outputs=output)
model.compile(optimizer=optimizers.Adam(learning_rate),
              loss=losses.CategoricalCrossentropy(from_logits=True),
              metrics=[metrics.CategoricalAccuracy()])

# Train
X, A_full = features, A_norm
history = model.fit([X, A_full], tf.one_hot(labels, depth=n_classes),
                    sample_weight=idx_train,
                    epochs=epochs, verbose=0,
                    validation_data=([X, A_full], tf.one_hot(labels, depth=n_classes)),
                    callbacks=[tf.keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(patience=patience, restore_best_weights=True)])

# Evaluate
y_pred = model.predict([X, A_full])[idx_test]
acc = np.mean(np.argmax(y_pred,1) == labels[idx_test])
print(f"Test accuracy: {acc:.4f}")

Summary

Implements a Graph Attention Network (GAT) in pure Keras for node classification on Cora citation graph. You gain experience with graph-based learning, multi-head attention, and non-Euclidean data.

# Input: full graph; Output: per-node predicted label distribution.
